sentence_stem: My friend sent me a message at midnight, so
correct_completion: I called her back right away.
full_sentence: My friend sent me a message at midnight, so I called her back right away.
acceptable_variants: I texted her back at once.

options.text: I called him back this morning.
options.why_wrong: 'Him' refers to a male person, but 'my friend' is female in this context. The object pronoun must match the person it refers to.

options.text: I called them back right away.
options.why_wrong: 'Them' is plural, but 'my friend' refers to one person, so a singular object pronoun is needed.

options.text: I called her back right away.
I called she back right away.
options.why_wrong: 'She' is a subject pronoun. After a verb, English needs an object pronoun such as 'her'.

grammar_focus: Object pronouns after verbs (me, him, her, them)
explanation: After a verb, English uses a separate object pronoun to show who receives the action, and the pronoun must agree with the person it refers to. Spanish speakers may find this pattern harder because Spanish object pronouns attach to the verb in some structures, which can lead to placing a subject pronoun in the object position.
translation: Mi amiga me envió un mensaje a medianoche, así que la llamé de vuelta enseguida.
